title: Hebrews Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hebrews chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hebrews Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hebrews Chapter 10.

questions.question: In Hebrews 10, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: For the law having a shadow of good things to come
In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure
Then said I, Lo, I come
But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever
questions.correctAnswer: For the law having a shadow of good things to come
questions.explanation: This is the first statement made in Hebrews 10, found in Hebrews 10:1.

questions.question: What can never make the comers perfect according to Hebrews 10?
options: The blood of bulls and goats
The sacrifices offered year by year
questions.correctAnswer: The sacrifices offered year by year
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:1 states that the law and its sacrifices can never make the comers perfect.

questions.question: What is remembered again in those sacrifices every year?
questions.correctAnswer: Sins
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:3 indicates that there is a remembrance made of sins every year in those sacrifices.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 10:4, what is not possible?
options: The blood of bulls and goats should take away sins
The offering of the body of Jesus Christ
The establishment of the second covenant
questions.correctAnswer: The blood of bulls and goats should take away sins
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:4 clearly states that it is not possible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

questions.question: What did He say when He came into the world?
options: I come to do thy will, O God
Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:5 records Him saying that sacrifice and offering were not desired.

questions.question: What has God had no pleasure in according to Hebrews 10:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt offerings
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:6 states that God has had no pleasure in burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin.

questions.question: What is written in the volume of the book?
options: To do thy will, O God
questions.correctAnswer: To do thy will, O God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:7 mentions that it is written that He comes to do God's will.

questions.question: What does He take away to establish the second?
questions.correctAnswer: The first covenant
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:9 states that He takes away the first to establish the second.

questions.question: Through what are we sanctified according to Hebrews 10:10?
options: The offering of the body of Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: The offering of the body of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:10 explains that we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What can never take away sins according to Hebrews 10:11?
questions.correctAnswer: The same sacrifices
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:11 states that the same sacrifices can never take away sins.

questions.question: What did He do after offering one sacrifice for sins forever?
options: Sat down on the right hand of God
questions.correctAnswer: Sat down on the right hand of God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:12 states that after offering one sacrifice for sins, He sat down at the right hand of God.

questions.question: True or False: The law had pleasure in burnt offerings.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:6 states that God had no pleasure in burnt offerings.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus Christ offered one sacrifice for sins forever.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:12 confirms that Jesus offered one sacrifice for sins for ever.

questions.question: True or False: The blood of bulls and goats can take away sins.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:4 states that it is not possible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

questions.question: True or False: The sacrifices were offered to please God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:8 indicates God had no pleasure in the sacrifices offered by the law.

medium.title: Hebrews Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hebrews Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 10:14, what has Jesus accomplished by one offering?
options: He hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified
He hath established a new covenant
He hath forgiven all sins temporarily
He hath given the law to believers
questions.correctAnswer: He hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:14 states that by one offering, Jesus hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 10:17 promise will happen if God puts His laws into the hearts and minds, as commanded in Hebrews 10:16?
options: Their sins and iniquities will be remembered no more
They will face judgment for their sins
They will be separated from God
questions.correctAnswer: Their sins and iniquities will be remembered no more
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:17 promises that when God puts His laws into their hearts and minds (Hebrews 10:16), He will remember their sins and iniquities no more.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 10:19 say believers have because of the blood of Jesus?
options: Boldness to enter into the holiest
questions.correctAnswer: Boldness to enter into the holiest
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:19 states that believers have boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 10:22-23, what are believers encouraged to do as a result of having a high priest over the house of God (Hebrews 10:21)?
options: Draw near with a true heart and hold fast the profession of faith
Avoid assembling together to keep faith private
questions.correctAnswer: Draw near with a true heart and hold fast the profession of faith
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:22-23 encourages believers to draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith and hold fast the profession of their faith, following the high priesthood mentioned in Hebrews 10:21.

questions.question: What practical instruction does Hebrews 10:24 give for Christian living?
options: Consider one another to provoke unto love and good works
questions.correctAnswer: Consider one another to provoke unto love and good works
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:24 instructs believers to consider one another to provoke unto love and good works as a practical aspect of Christian living.

questions.question: What warning does Hebrews 10:25 give about forsaking assembling together?
options: It discourages exhorting one another as the day approaches
It is the manner of some and should be avoided
questions.correctAnswer: It is the manner of some and should be avoided
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:25 warns that forsaking assembling together is the manner of some and urges believers not to do so but to exhort one another.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 10:18, what is true where remission of sins has occurred?
options: There is no more offering for sin
questions.correctAnswer: There is no more offering for sin
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:18 states that where remission of sins is, there is no more offering for sin.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 10:20 mean by Jesus consecrating a 'new and living way' through the veil?
options: He opened access to God through his flesh
He established a new law replacing the old
He removed the need for faith
questions.correctAnswer: He opened access to God through his flesh
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:20 explains that Jesus consecrated a new and living way through the veil, which is his flesh, opening access to God.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 10:23 encourage believers to do regarding their faith?
options: Hold fast the profession of their faith without wavering
questions.correctAnswer: Hold fast the profession of their faith without wavering
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:23 encourages believers to hold fast the profession of their faith without wavering because God is faithful.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 10:22, what are believers to have when they draw near with a true heart?
questions.correctAnswer: Full assurance of faith
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:22 instructs believers to draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith.

questions.question: What is the effect of having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience according to Hebrews 10:22?
options: We can draw near to God with confidence
We must continue offering animal sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: We can draw near to God with confidence
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:22 implies that having hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience allows believers to draw near to God confidently.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 10:26 describe the consequence of sinning willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth?
options: There remaineth no more sacrifice for sins
questions.correctAnswer: There remaineth no more sacrifice for sins
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:26 clearly states that if one sins willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 10:24 instructs believers to provoke one another unto love and good works.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:24 instructs believers to consider one another to provoke unto love and good works, confirming the statement.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 10:25 encourages believers to forsake assembling together as a sign of strong faith.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:25 instructs believers not to forsake assembling together but to exhort one another, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: According to Hebrews 10:18, where sins are forgiven, continual offerings for sin must still be made.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:18 states that where remission of sins is, there is no more offering for sin, so continual offerings are not required.

hard.title: Hebrews Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hebrews Chapter 10.

questions.question: What will devour the adversaries according to Hebrews 10:27?
options: A certain fearful looking for of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: A certain fearful looking for of judgment
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Hebrews 10:27 states, 'But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.'

questions.question: According to Hebrews 10:28, what was the consequence for those who despised Moses' law?
questions.correctAnswer: They died without mercy
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as Hebrews 10:28 states, 'He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses.'

questions.question: In Hebrews 10:29, what is compared to the punishment for those who have trodden under foot the Son of God?
questions.correctAnswer: A greater punishment
questions.explanation: The verse implies that the punishment for those who disrespect the Son of God is of 'how much sorer punishment' than that for those who despised Moses' law in Hebrews 10:29.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 10:31 say about falling into the hands of God?
questions.correctAnswer: It is a fearful thing
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:31 states, 'It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God,' indicating the seriousness of judgment.

questions.question: What must one have after doing the will of God according to Hebrews 10:36?
questions.correctAnswer: Patience
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:36 states, 'For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 10:39 affirm about those who believe?
options: They are not of them who draw back unto perdition
questions.correctAnswer: They are not of them who draw back unto perdition
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'punishment' (Hebrews 10:29) mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Chastisement
questions.explanation: The Greek word often translated as 'punishment' in this context refers to chastisement or corrective action, emphasizing the seriousness of sin against God.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Hebrews 10:30 with the phrase 'Vengeance belongeth unto me'?
questions.correctAnswer: Quotation
questions.explanation: This phrase is a quotation from the Old Testament, emphasizing the authority of God in enacting vengeance.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of judgment in Hebrews 10:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 20:12
questions.explanation: This passage describes the judgment before the great white throne, echoing the theme of divine judgment found in Hebrews 10:27.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage parallels the concept of mercy and judgment in Hebrews 10:28?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 19:15
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 19:15 discusses the law regarding witnesses, paralleling the context of judgment in Hebrews 10:28.

questions.question: What comes before the warning in Hebrews 10:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Exhortation to hold fast
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:26 serves as a warning about willful sin, leading into the fearful consequences described in verse 27.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'the just shall live by faith' in Hebrews 10:38?
options: It is a call to action
It is a quote from Habakkuk
It refers to the old covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It is a quote from Habakkuk
questions.explanation: This phrase directly quotes Habakkuk 2:4, emphasizing the continuity of faith's importance throughout Scripture.

questions.question: The idea that 'there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins' in Hebrews 10:26 is a warning against what?
questions.correctAnswer: Willful sin
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:26 warns that if one sins willfully after receiving knowledge of the truth, there is no more sacrifice, highlighting the seriousness of rebellion against God.

questions.question: It is true that Hebrews 10:34 encourages believers to have compassion?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For ye had compassion of me in my bonds,' encouraging believers to show compassion as a mark of faith.

questions.question: It is false that Hebrews 10:32 mentions enduring a fight of afflictions after illumination?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:32 clearly states that after being illuminated, believers endured a great fight of afflictions, making this statement false.

theological.title: Hebrews Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hebrews Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 10:1 teach about the limitation of the Mosaic Law in relation to salvation?
options: The law provides a complete and perfect means to make sinners perfect
The law is only a shadow and cannot perfect those who come to God
The law abolishes the need for sacrifice
The law is the final covenant between God and man
questions.correctAnswer: The law is only a shadow and cannot perfect those who come to God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:1 explains that the law is a shadow of good things to come and cannot make the comers perfect with yearly sacrifices, emphasizing its temporary and incomplete nature.

questions.question: What doctrine about the efficacy of animal sacrifices is taught in Hebrews 10:4?
options: The blood of bulls and goats takes away sins permanently
Animal sacrifices are sufficient for eternal cleansing
The blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins
Sacrifices are unnecessary for forgiveness of sins
questions.correctAnswer: The blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:4 clearly states that it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins, highlighting the insufficiency of animal sacrifices for true atonement.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning sanctification is taught in Hebrews 10:10?
options: Sanctification is through the offering of Jesus Christ’s body once for all
Sanctification is achieved by human effort
Sanctification is unrelated to Christ’s sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification is through the offering of Jesus Christ’s body once for all
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:10 teaches that by the will of God we are sanctified through the one-time offering of Jesus’ body, emphasizing the sufficiency and finality of Christ’s sacrifice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 10:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Forgiveness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:17 states that God will remember their sins and iniquities no more, demonstrating His attribute of forgiveness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Hebrews 10:30?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:30 quotes God declaring vengeance and that He will judge His people, highlighting His attribute of justice.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 10:19-20 connect to the Old Testament tabernacle and Christ’s priestly role?
options: It denies any connection between Christ and the tabernacle
It shows Christ as the new high priest who opens a new and living way through His flesh, fulfilling the veil’s symbolism
It teaches that the tabernacle sacrifices remain necessary
It portrays the veil as a symbol of human sinfulness without redemption
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Christ as the new high priest who opens a new and living way through His flesh, fulfilling the veil’s symbolism
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:19-20 speaks of boldness to enter the holiest by the blood of Jesus through a new and living way consecrated through His flesh, connecting Christ’s priesthood to the Old Testament tabernacle veil.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Hebrews 10:25 make concerning Christian community?
options: It discourages assembling to avoid persecution
It emphasizes the importance of persistent fellowship and exhortation as the day of Christ’s return approaches
It prioritizes individual faith over community
It teaches that assembling was only necessary in the early church
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the importance of persistent fellowship and exhortation as the day of Christ’s return approaches
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:25 exhorts believers not to forsake assembling but to encourage one another especially as the Day approaches, linking Christian community to eschatological hope.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 10:11 and 10:12 teach about the priestly sacrifice?
options: Repeated sacrifices by priests are sufficient for sin removal
Christ’s single sacrifice replaces the repeated, ineffective sacrifices of the Levitical priests
The priestly sacrifices and Christ’s sacrifice are unrelated
The priesthood remains unchanged under the new covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s single sacrifice replaces the repeated, ineffective sacrifices of the Levitical priests
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:11 explains that priests offer the same sacrifices daily which cannot take away sins, while verse 12 highlights Christ’s one sacrifice for all, establishing the superiority of His priesthood.

questions.question: What doctrine about covenant fulfillment is taught by the synthesis of Hebrews 10:16 and 10:17?
options: The covenant involves external laws only
God promises internal transformation and complete forgiveness of sins
The covenant does not involve forgiveness
The covenant is conditional on human works
questions.correctAnswer: God promises internal transformation and complete forgiveness of sins
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:16 speaks of God writing His laws on hearts and minds, and 10:17 promises God will remember sins no more, together teaching the new covenant’s internal and forgiving nature.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about faith and perseverance is revealed in Hebrews 10:23 and 10:36?
options: Believers must hold fast their faith and patiently endure to receive God’s promises
The promise is received before doing God’s will
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must hold fast their faith and patiently endure to receive God’s promises
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:23 urges holding fast without wavering, and 10:36 teaches the need for patience to obtain the promise, together emphasizing persevering faith.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth do Hebrews 10:26 and 10:27 teach about the consequences of willful sin after receiving the truth?
options: There remains a sacrifice for willful sin
Willful sin after knowledge of the truth results in no further sacrifice and fearful judgment
Such sin is easily forgiven without consequence
Judgment is avoided if one repents later
questions.correctAnswer: Willful sin after knowledge of the truth results in no further sacrifice and fearful judgment
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:26 states no more sacrifice remains for willful sin after knowing the truth, and 10:27 describes fearful judgment awaiting such adversaries.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Hebrews 10:28-31 teaches God’s judgment is arbitrary and severe without warning. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God judges without any prior warnings or witnesses
God’s judgment is based on deliberate rejection of covenant and grace, with warnings given through law and Spirit
Judgment is random and unrelated to sin
God’s judgment is always immediate and harsh regardless of circumstances
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is based on deliberate rejection of covenant and grace, with warnings given through law and Spirit
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:28 references judgment under law with witnesses, and 10:29-31 explains harsher punishment for those who reject the Son of God and the Spirit of grace, indicating judgment is just and preceded by revelation.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christian suffering and hope is taught in Hebrews 10:32-34?
options: Christian suffering is meaningless and to be avoided
Suffering is endured with joy because of hope in a better, eternal substance in heaven
Believers should not associate with those who suffer
questions.correctAnswer: Suffering is endured with joy because of hope in a better, eternal substance in heaven
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:32-34 recalls believers’ endurance of affliction and joyful acceptance of loss, because they knew they possessed an enduring heavenly substance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Hebrews 10:23 through the exhortation to hold fast the profession of faith without wavering?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:23 emphasizes God’s faithfulness in fulfilling His promises, encouraging believers to hold fast confidently without wavering.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 10:22 teach about the means by which believers approach God in the new covenant?
options: By strict adherence to the law without faith
With a true heart, full assurance of faith, hearts sprinkled from evil conscience, and bodies washed with pure water
questions.correctAnswer: With a true heart, full assurance of faith, hearts sprinkled from evil conscience, and bodies washed with pure water
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:22 describes believers drawing near God sincerely and confidently, cleansed both inwardly and outwardly, symbolizing the new covenant approach.
